title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
summary: How much does an algorithm's running-time distribution under independent randomness reveal about its behavior when independence is no longer guaranteed? We study sources satisfying $ν[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$. The constraint controls complete-prefix probabilities while allowing individual choices to be predictable, even fully determined by the past.
